steps.body: Every angle sorts into one of four families, compared to two benchmarks — 90° and 180°. **Acute:** less than 90°. **Right:** exactly 90°. **Obtuse:** between 90° and 180°. **Straight:** exactly 180°.
Open an angle just beyond a square corner.

widget.prompt: Open the rays to 110°. Watch the angle move past the 90° right-angle mark.
widget.successFeedback: 110° is wider than 90° and narrower than 180°, so it is obtuse.
widget.lowFeedback: The angle is still below 110°. Open it wider.
widget.highFeedback: The angle is above 110°. Bring the ray back.

predict.prompt: An angle just slightly WIDER than a square corner — acute or obtuse?
predict.reveal: The square corner is the border at 90° — anything past it, even a hair, is obtuse (up until straight at 180°); anything short of it is acute. The families split at that line.

explanationVariants: It's bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight one.

widget.prompt: What family does a 150° angle belong to?

options.label: Obtuse — between 90° and 180°
options.feedback: 150 sits between the 90° and 180° benchmarks — obtuse.

options.label: Acute — less than 90°
options.feedback: Acute angles are UNDER 90°. 150 is well past that — it's obtuse.

options.label: Right — exactly 90°
options.feedback: A right angle is exactly 90°. 150 is bigger than that — obtuse.

options.label: Straight — exactly 180°
options.feedback: A straight angle is exactly 180°. 150 is short of that — obtuse.

steps.body: The boundaries are **exact**, not approximate. 90° is always right — never 'almost right.' 89° and 91° are both a full family away from 90°: acute and obtuse. One degree can flip the classification.

explanationVariants: 89° is one less than 90 — still under the right-angle benchmark, so it's acute.
Only exactly 90° counts as a right angle.

widget.prompt: Is an 89° angle acute or right?

options.label: Acute — it's just under 90°
options.feedback: 89 is less than 90, so it's acute — not 'almost right.'

options.label: Right — it's basically 90°
options.feedback: Right angles are EXACTLY 90°, never approximately. 89 is under that: acute.

options.label: Both, since it's so close
options.feedback: An angle belongs to exactly one family. 89 is under 90, so it's acute, not right.

options.label: Obtuse, since it's a big-looking number
options.feedback: 89 is still under the 90° right-angle benchmark, so it's acute, not obtuse.

widget.prompt: Sort these angles, paying close attention to the exact numbers.

items.feedback: 179 is just under 180 — still obtuse, not straight.

widget.missFeedback: Compare each number to 90 exactly — even one degree changes the family.
widget.successFeedback: 89° and 60° are acute; 91° and 179° are obtuse — the boundary is exact.

explanationVariants: 179° is just short of 180°, so it's still obtuse, not straight.

widget.prompt: Is a 179° angle obtuse or straight?

options.label: Obtuse — it's just under 180°
options.feedback: 179 is less than 180, so it's still obtuse — not 'basically straight.'

options.label: Straight — it's basically 180°
options.feedback: Straight angles are EXACTLY 180°. 179 falls one short — still obtuse.

options.label: Acute, since it's a familiar-looking number
options.feedback: 179 is far past 90° — nowhere near acute. It's obtuse, just short of straight.

options.label: Right, since it's close to a common benchmark
options.feedback: Right angles are exactly 90° — 179 isn't close to that at all. It's obtuse.

hints: A ladder leaning to form an angle of exactly 90° with the ground would be perfectly upright.
This ladder's angle is 75°, less than that.
explanationVariants: 75° is less than the 90° right-angle benchmark, so the ladder's angle is acute.
Falling short of 90° places it in the acute family.

widget.prompt: A ladder leans against a wall, forming a 75° angle with the ground. What family is this angle?

options.label: Acute — 75° is less than 90°
options.feedback: 75 falls short of the 90° right-angle benchmark — acute.

options.label: Right — close enough to 90°
options.feedback: Right angles are exactly 90°. 75 is 15° short of that — it's acute, not right.

options.label: Obtuse — it looks tilted
options.feedback: Obtuse angles are OVER 90°. 75 is under 90 — it's acute.

options.label: Straight — the ladder forms a line with the ground
options.feedback: A straight angle would mean the ladder lies flat (180°). Leaning at 75° is acute.

takeaways: Acute is under 90°; right is exactly 90°; obtuse is between 90° and 180°; straight is exactly 180°.
The 90° and 180° boundaries are exact — one degree flips the family.
Every angle belongs to exactly one of the four families.
steps.teaser: next chapter: angles that combine to build a bigger one.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Compare the degree number to 90 and 180.** Under 90 is acute. Exactly 90 is right. Between 90 and 180 is obtuse. Exactly 180 is straight. For 30°: it's under 90, so acute.

explanationVariants: It falls in the smallest family.

widget.prompt: What family does a 30° angle belong to?

options.label: Right
options.feedback: Right is exactly 90°. 30 is far under that — acute.

options.label: Obtuse
options.feedback: Obtuse is OVER 90°. 30 is well under — acute.
